repairs.text: Strongest feature: Hernandez uses the red-ball example to distinguish fallible external color judgment from accurate awareness that a reddish experience occurred even after illumination reveals an orange object, directly answering the appeal to induced or misleading experiences. Principal limitation: This contrast establishes neither that conscious experience differs from its neural realization nor that introspection is entirely error-proof, because mental states can be misdescribed even when experience unquestionably occurs. Live burden: Hernandez must identify a property of conscious occurrence that no neural representational process could possess, then explain why that difference requires an immaterial substantial bearer rather than merely separating appearance from represented reality. Locked score: The locked score of 74 fits a clear, responsive example, while its ultimate identity target and proposed soul-level consequence remain evidentially underdetermined.

Strongest feature: Aron Ra supplies the negative’s clearest positive account of rational warrant, explaining how confidence improves when impressions are checked against experience, other observers, independent data, counterevidence, and tests asking what fact would disconfirm a claim. Principal limitation: These practical error-correction procedures do not fully answer Hernandez’s deeper challenge about how physically caused reasoning possesses normative authority rather than simply producing conclusions determined by causal history. Live burden: Aron Ra must establish that reliable, reasons-responsive inference supplies the intellectual integrity rational judgment requires, while explaining why an additional uncaused subject would contribute no further reliability to these checking procedures. Locked score: The locked score of 84 reflects a coherent, concrete, strongly warranted, directly responsive, and correction-ready alternative, tempered only by compressed treatment of normativity’s metaphysical grounding.
